ACT I

SCENE I. A chamber at evening.

FIRST SPEAKER.
Thou hast the letter, and thou dost not read it.
What dost thou fear that paper should declare?
The hour is late; the candle burns to nothing;
And yet thou standest as a man of stone.

SECOND SPEAKER.
I have the letter, and I know its hand.
That which I fear is written plain within,
And having read it once I need not twice.
Thou art too quick to counsel what thou know'st not.

FIRST SPEAKER.
Then give it me, and let me bear the weight,
For thou hast borne enough of it this month.
A grief divided is a grief the lighter,
And what thou carriest alone will break thee.

SECOND SPEAKER.
Thou canst not bear it. It is mine to bear.
The name upon the seal is mine, and thine
Is nowhere in the matter. Go to bed.
I shall be well enough by morning light.

FIRST SPEAKER.
Thou wilt not. I have watched thee three nights running,
And every night thou sayest the selfsame thing,
And every morning findest thee the worse.
What is it that thou hidest from a friend?

SECOND SPEAKER.
A debt. A promise made and never kept.
A word I gave when I was young and foolish,
Which now returns to ask what I have not.
There. Thou hast it. Art thou better pleased?

FIRST SPEAKER.
I am not pleased. I am the less afraid,
Which is a kind of gladness in its way.
A debt may yet be paid. A word recalled.
Come; we shall find the means between us two.
